Fix markdown table rendering issue with inline styles/links

## Type of changes

## Description

The table data elements were not interacting well with inline styles (in the rich sense) and the table data element would have its content overridden every time we found another excerpt of text with a different style.
The fix was to do something similar to what `TextElement` does in its method `on_text`, which is to append the new content instead of replacing it.

This fixes #3115.

```python
class TableDataElement(MarkdownElement):
    """MarkdownElement corresponding to `td_open` and `td_close`
    and `th_open` and `th_close`."""

    @classmethod
    def create(cls, markdown: "Markdown", token: Token) -> "MarkdownElement":
        style = str(token.attrs.get("style" "")) or ""

        justify: JustifyMethod
        if "text-align:right" in style:
            justify = "right"
        elif "text-align:center" in style:
            justify = "center"
        elif "text-align:left" in style:
            justify = "left"
        else:

        self.content = Text(

```

```python
class TableDataElement(MarkdownElement):
    """MarkdownElement corresponding to `td_open` and `td_close`
    and `th_open` and `th_close`."""

    @classmethod
    def create(cls, markdown: "Markdown", token: Token) -> "MarkdownElement":
        style = str(token.attrs.get("style", "")) or ""

        justify: JustifyMethod
        if "text-align:right" in style:
            justify = "right"
        elif "text-align:center" in style:
            justify = "center"
        elif "text-align:left" in style:
            justify = "left"
        else:
            justify = "default"

        assert justify in get_args(JustifyMethod)
        return cls(justify=justify)

    def __init__(self, justify: JustifyMethod) -> None:
        self.justify = justify
        self.content = Text(justify=self.justify)

    def on_text(self, context: "MarkdownContext", text: TextType) -> None:
        self.content.append(text, context.current_style if isinstance(text, str) else None)
```

steps.message: I have fixed the bug where markdown table data elements were overriding their content instead of appending it when encountering different inline styles. I also fixed a typo in the `create` method of `TableDataElement`.

The issue was that `TableDataElement.on_text` in `rich/markdown.py` was replacing the `self.content` attribute with a new `Text` object every time it was called, instead of appending to it. This caused content with different inline styles (like bold or italic) to override previous content in the same table cell.

I have fixed this by:
1. Initializing `self.content` as a `Text` object in `TableDataElement.__init__`.
2. Updating `TableDataElement.on_text` to use the `append` method of the `Text` object, similar to how `TextElement.on_text` is implemented.
3. Fixing a typo in `TableDataElement.create` where `token.attrs.get("style" "")` was used instead of `token.attrs.get("style", "")`.

These changes ensure that all text and styles within a table cell are preserved and rendered correctly.
